theorem.statement:
For every fixed known \(x_0\in[0,1]^d\), every \(n\ge2\), and every fixed parameter tuple satisfying \(S\le S_\star\), the construction \(\mathfrak H_{n,x_0}^{\mathrm{comp}}\) supplies deterministic scales and amplitudes \(0<\ell\le h\le1\) and \(a,b>0\), constants \(0<c\le C<\infty\) depending only on \((d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\), and two finite priors \(\Pi_+\) and \(\Pi_-\) supported on \(\mathcal P(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\) with the following properties.  The target \(\tau_P(x_0)\) is constant under each prior, with values \(\theta_+\) and \(\theta_-\) satisfying
\[
 |\theta_+-\theta_-|\ge c\rho_n.
\]
Writing
\[
 \mathsf M_\varepsilon=\int P_O^{\otimes n}\,d\Pi_\varepsilon(P),
 \qquad \varepsilon\in\{+,-\},
\]
for the actual fixed-\(n\) product mixtures, one has
\[
 H^2(\mathsf M_+,\mathsf M_-)\le
 Cn^2h^d\ell^da^2b^2\le\frac14.
\]
Conditional on the covariates, the shared-sign graph factorization has exactly equal singleton mixtures, \(Q_{1,+}=Q_{1,-}\), and every component of size \(r\ge2\) satisfies the uniform inequality
\[
 H^2(Q_{r,+},Q_{r,-})\le Ca^2b^2r^4(9/2)^r.
\]
Every law in both prior supports has the exact uniform covariate law on \([0,1]^d\).  Thus the certificate deletes no support and uses neither conditioning on a favorable occupancy event nor Poissonization.
theorem.proof_tex:
Fix \(x_0\in[0,1]^d\), \(n\ge2\), and a parameter tuple with \(S\le S_\star\).  Apply \(\mathrm{lem:closed\mbox{-}regime\mbox{-}fixed\mbox{-}point\mbox{-}component\mbox{-}mixtures}\) at this \(x_0\), this \(n\), and this tuple.  That result supplies two finite priors \(\Pi_+\) and \(\Pi_-\), supported on \(\mathcal P(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\), and constants and tuning quantities depending only on the fixed tuple and uniformly in \(x_0\).  Its target-separation conclusion is exactly
\[
 |\theta_+-\theta_-|\ge c\rho_n. \tag{1}
\]
For \(\varepsilon\in\{+,-\}\), define the fixed-product mixture
\[
 \mathsf M_\varepsilon
 =\int P_O^{\otimes n}\,d\Pi_\varepsilon(P). \tag{2}
\]
The same result states that the conditional sign mixtures agree on every singleton component and, uniformly for every component size \(r\ge2\), obey
\[
 Q_{1,+}=Q_{1,-},
 \qquad
 H^2(Q_{r,+},Q_{r,-})\le Ca^2b^2r^4(9/2)^r. \tag{3}
\]
Its component-factorization and spanning-tree conclusion gives, for the mixtures in (2),
\[
 H^2(\mathsf M_+,\mathsf M_-)
 \le Cn^2h^d\ell^da^2b^2
 \le\frac14. \tag{4}
\]
Finally, the invoked result places every prior atom in the same class \(\mathcal P(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L)\), retains the exact uniform covariate marginal on the full cube, and obtains (4) directly for \(P_O^{\otimes n}\), without an occupancy-event restriction or a Poissonized experiment.  Equations (1)--(4) are all the requested parts of the all-\(x_0\), fixed-\(n\) component-mixture certificate, so the answer to the open-ended question is affirmative.
theorem.justification: This theorem records the affirmative all-\(x_0\) answer to the fixed-\(n\) component-mixture question as a direct consequence of the established component certificate.
theorem.gap: One-observation mixture cancellation alone does not control a shared-prior product likelihood; the invoked component theorem supplies the exact singleton cancellation, component affinity estimate, and full graph sum in the stipulated experiment.
theorem.consumer: The certificate is the fixed-product lower-bound input used by the sharp exact-uniform pointwise CATE minimax theorem.

prose_updates.related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE is the closest comparator: its lower theorem covers a broader bounded-density class and its upper theorem requires additional design and nuisance-estimation conditions, whereas the present result closes the fixed-\(n\) converse and matching upper bound on the strict exact-uniform bounded-overlap Bernoulli/interiority subclass. The lower converse therefore transfers upward by subclass inclusion to any broader model that contains this subclass and uses the same point target; the exact-uniform upper proof does not transfer in that direction and is not claimed there. RobinsTchetgenLiVanderVaart2009SemiparametricMinimax supplies the product-mixture perspective, but the shared smooth frames here require random overlap-component factorization rather than a deterministic coordinate-local partition. ShenGaoWittenHan2020Variance is a random-design nonlinear-functional analogue for repeated local occupancy. Kennedy2023DRCATE and NieWager2021RLearner provide oracle-facing upper comparisons, while RobinsLiTchetgenVanderVaart2008HOIF motivates the finite projection correction. LiuMukherjeeRobinsTchetgen2021Adaptive studies adaptive nonlinear-functional estimation, whereas the present estimator uses known smoothness. LeeOkuiWhang2017CATEBands studies uniform CATE confidence bands, whereas this note proves pointwise mean-risk only. AtheyWager2021PolicyLearning studies policy-value and regret learning rather than pointwise CATE minimax precision. ChernozhukovWuthrichZhu2021Conformal studies conformal counterfactual and synthetic-control inference rather than this estimand or guarantee. WagerAthey2018CausalForests is an application-facing consumer: this is a precision benchmark for \(\texttt{causal\_forest}\) and R-learner workflows, not a claim that existing forests attain the bound.
